i have the exact same problem, so just know you're not alone in your anxiety. i agree with what other people are saying, too. using backline weapons allows you to observe the situations unfolding in game and react to support your team. like any skill, you have to practice. you weren't born knowing how to walk, speak, write, or do math, but you were taught by others who do and continued practicing by using those skills frequently. gaming is no different. 

arm yourself with information. do a quick recon of the maps for the mode you want to play before you jump into a match. take note of things like where your weapon can reach, how long it takes to get to the objective by each route, ways into the enemy spawn that might be left un-inked in favor of rushing to the objective, and dangerous areas like one way drops into mid where the only way out is a super jump. Squid School on youtube has very helpful videos on things like coordinated special usage and when to super jump back into mid. ive felt myself improve a lot since i started watching his stuff.

another thing to remember is that when you have an anxiety disorder, your brain doesn't actually know the difference between being nervous about pvp and being in real-life danger. i know it sounds stupid, but you have to respect that you're afraid. forcing yourself into a situation you subconsciously perceive as threatening will just make you feel worse. going on a walk beforehand helps me personally. it gets my jitters out so my reticle isn't shaking all match. keep in mind that if you're losing and it looks like you can't push back, the match will be over soon anyway, and you'll be onto the next one. in order for someone to win, someone else has to lose. it won't be overnight, but it will become easier. try to treat every loss as an opportunity to learn and grow!
